comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Cause established: reading (a), runner contention -- NOT a leaked process/handle.

Decisive evidence from run 33846424069, job 100939218689:

* the failure is subprocess.TimeoutExpired on `git rev-parse HEAD` after 5s, with
  `<Popen: returncode: -9 ...>` -- the child was ALIVE and killed by the timeout, so it
  was running, not wedged on a git resource.
* the same run emitted 400 [rebar-ci-timing] warnings (threshold 1.0s), topping out at
  `built_distributions fixture_setup elapsed=4.562s` on a DIFFERENT worker (gw1). Ordinary
  fixture setup on that runner reaches 91% of the probe's fixed 5s bound.

Reading (b) has no mechanism, and the ticket's premise for it is factually wrong:

* the blamed test drives a shell STUB npm (_SUCCEEDS: `mkdir -p node_modules; exit 0`)
  under tmp_path. It does NOT provision a real Node toolchain -- it is one of the cheapest
  tests in the file. There is no real npm ci/esbuild child to leak.
* `git rev-parse HEAD` reads .git/HEAD plus refs and takes NO lock, so no leaked handle can
  serialize against it.
* patched-clock ruled out: CPython binds `from time import monotonic as _time` in
  subprocess, so the timeout check is immune to a time.monotonic patch.
* leaked PATH ruled out experimentally: monkeypatch (function-scoped, non-autouse) is
  finalized BEFORE the autouse guard's post-yield, so the probe runs with the session PATH.

So the defect is the BOUND, not the test. Fix: _run_git_probe re-samples a timed-out
attempt up to GIT_PROBE_ATTEMPTS (3); the final attempt sits outside the retry loop so a
PERSISTENT timeout still raises loudly. No sleep between attempts (the elapsed per-attempt
timeout is the backoff, and sleeping would re-introduce the patched-time.sleep hazard
_stable_subprocess_time defends against).

Guard not weakened, and it is enforced: mutating head/porcelain to swallow TimeoutExpired
fails 3 tests. A real HEAD move is still detected. The e2e test is untouched.

Gerrit change 2618: https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2618
Verification dispatch: https://github.com/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/33855430270

FIXED AND PROVEN. Change 2618: https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2618 -- LLM-Review +1, plan review PASS with 0 blocking.

WORKFLOW_DISPATCH PROOF (run 33855430270, ref bug-860b-macos-git-probe, job 100967566130):
  sweep (macos, full suite) = SUCCESS
  before (main 6b034b9f8224): 19243 passed, 72 skipped, 422 warnings, 1 ERROR in 2687.89s
  after  (this fix):          19244 passed, 72 skipped, 460 warnings, 0 errors in 2707.41s
The +1 test is the new regression test. Verified against the actual schedule-gated job rather than
inferred.

MY PREMISE IN THIS TICKET WAS WRONG AND THE IMPLEMENTER CHECKED RATHER THAN INHERITING IT. I wrote
that the blamed test 'provisions a real Node toolchain (npm ci plus an esbuild bundle) and is the
heaviest thing in the suite'. It does not. It drives a shell STUB npm ('mkdir -p node_modules; exit
0') under tmp_path and is one of the CHEAPEST tests in the file. I was right that the cause was
contention and wrong about the mechanism, and my wrong mechanism would have sent a fix at the test.

READING (a) SETTLED ON EVIDENCE, not elimination:
 - '<Popen: returncode: -9 ...>' in the traceback -- the child was ALIVE and killed by the timeout.
   Running, not wedged.
 - 400 [rebar-ci-timing] warnings in that same run (threshold 1.0s), topping out at
   'built_distributions fixture_setup elapsed=4.562s' on a DIFFERENT worker. Ordinary fixture setup
   on that runner reaches 91% OF THE PROBE'S FIXED 5s BOUND. The bound sits inside the runner's own
   latency distribution.
So the defect is THE BOUND, not the test: one fixed-timeout sample of a read-only, idempotent probe
taken ~19,000 times, three xdist workers deep, across a 45-minute run.

READING (b) RULED OUT AT MECHANISM LEVEL rather than by assertion: there is no real npm/esbuild child
to leak; 'git rev-parse HEAD' reads .git/HEAD and refs and takes NO LOCK, so no leaked handle can
serialize against it; a patched clock is impossible because CPython binds 'from time import monotonic
as _time' in subprocess; and a leaked PATH was ruled out EXPERIMENTALLY -- monkeypatch is
function-scoped and non-autouse, so it finalizes before the autouse guard's post-yield.

THE FIX, and one design choice worth preserving: _run_git_probe re-samples a timed-out attempt up to
GIT_PROBE_ATTEMPTS = 3, with THE FINAL ATTEMPT OUTSIDE THE RETRY LOOP so a persistent TimeoutExpired
propagates unconditionally -- 'loudness is structural, not a conditional a later edit could invert'.
And no sleep between attempts: the elapsed per-attempt timeout IS the backoff, and sleeping would
re-introduce the patched-time.sleep hazard that _stable_subprocess_time exists to defend against.

AC4 HONOURED: the e2e test is untouched -- not skipped, not marked, not excluded. The fix is in the
probe, which is where the defect actually was.

AC3 verified by mutation: making head/porcelain swallow TimeoutExpired FAILS 3 tests, and
test_head_detects_a_commit / test_guard_fails_a_test_that_commits still detect a real HEAD move. The
guard is not weakened.

Defect-seeded RED in 25 seconds rather than a 45-minute run:
  subprocess.TimeoutExpired: Command '[git, -C, .../repo, rev-parse, HEAD]' timed out after 0.484s
  FAILED test_a_transient_probe_stall_is_re_sampled_rather_than_reported
GREEN with the fix: 23 passed.

Gates: make lint exit 0; make typecheck clean (755 files); the three pytest-only gates 54 passed (run
after git add); tests/unit + tests/e2e 15391 passed. No new mechanism.

Verified -1 comes SOLELY from scanner-integration (90c7, another session). Not closing until that

compiled_state.description:
## Symptom

`sweep (macos, full suite)` fails on `main` at `6b034b9f8224` (run `33846424069`). The job has no
`continue-on-error` (`.github/workflows/test.yml:370-373`), so it reddens the branch head.

```
19243 passed, 72 skipped, 422 warnings, 1 error in 2687.89s (0:44:47)
ERROR tests/e2e/test_toolchain_provisioning.py::test_provisioning_installs_then_builds_and_leaves_the_bundle_in_place
  - subprocess.TimeoutExpired: Command '['git', '-C', '/Users/runner/work/rebar/rebar', 'rev-parse', 'HEAD']'
    timed out after 5 seconds
```

The test itself PASSES. The error is in the autouse `_no_repo_commits` guard's post-test probe
(`tests/conftest.py:774` -> `tests/_isolation.py:68,39`).

## Root cause (established, not assumed)

The cause is **runner contention**, not a leaked process/handle, and not the named test.

1. The premise that this test provisions a real Node toolchain is **false**. It drives a shell
   **stub** `npm` (`_SUCCEEDS`: `mkdir -p node_modules; exit 0`) under `tmp_path`. It is one of the
   cheapest tests in the file. There is no real `npm ci`/esbuild child to leak.
2. `git rev-parse HEAD` reads `.git/HEAD` plus refs and takes **no lock**. No leaked handle or child
   process can serialize against it, so the leaked-handle reading has no mechanism.
3. A patched clock is ruled out: CPython binds `from time import monotonic as _time` in
   `subprocess`, so `subprocess.run`'s timeout check is immune to a `time.monotonic` patch.
4. A leaked `PATH` is ruled out experimentally: `monkeypatch` (function-scoped, non-autouse) is
   finalized BEFORE the autouse guard's post-yield, so the probe runs with the session `PATH`.
5. `Popen: returncode: -9` shows the child was alive and killed by the timeout -- it was running,
   not wedged on a git-specific resource.
6. The same run emitted **400** `[rebar-ci-timing]` warnings (threshold 1.0s), topping out at
   `built_distributions fixture_setup elapsed=4.562s` on a different worker. Ordinary fixture setup
   on this runner reaches **91% of the probe's fixed 5s bound**.

So the defect is the **bound**, not the test: `GIT_PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 5` is a single-sample
fixed bound on a read-only idempotent probe that runs ~19,000 times under `-n 3` on a 45-minute
macOS runner. 5s sits inside that runner's observed latency distribution, so the guard reports an
infrastructure stall as a test ERROR.

## Approach

Make the probe **resilient**, not lenient. `git rev-parse HEAD` and `git status --porcelain` are
read-only and idempotent, so a `TimeoutExpired` may simply be re-sampled: retry the probe up to
`GIT_PROBE_ATTEMPTS` times, with no sleep between attempts -- the elapsed per-attempt timeout is
itself the backoff, and adding a sleep would re-introduce the patched-`time.sleep` hazard that
`_stable_subprocess_time` exists to avoid.

A **persistent** timeout still raises, unchanged. That is deliberate: `_isolation.head` already
re-raises `TimeoutExpired` so the guard fails loudly rather than silently ceasing to detect a HEAD
move, and that property must survive -- it is the "absence of execution reported as success" trap.
The change absorbs a **transient** stall and leaves the **persistent** failure loud.

Explicitly not doing: skipping or marking the test on macOS (the test is innocent, and a skip would
hide it), and not merely raising the per-attempt timeout (a re-exec is strictly better than a longer
wait on one possibly-starved process).

## Scope

- `tests/_isolation.py` -- `_run_git_probe` gains the bounded retry and `GIT_PROBE_ATTEMPTS`.
- `tests/unit/test_repo_isolation_guard.py` -- the `_blocking_git` shim gains the ability to block
  every probe from a given call onward (persistent) as well as exactly one (transient), plus the new
  tests below.

No `src/` change. `tests/conftest.py` and `tests/e2e/test_toolchain_provisioning.py` are NOT
modified: the guard's caller and the innocent test both stay as they are.

## Testing

- `pytest tests/unit/test_repo_isolation_guard.py` -- the guard's self-test suite, including:
  - a NEW test that a **transient** probe stall (one blocked call, then a responsive git) is
    absorbed and `head()` returns the correct sha -- RED before the fix (`TimeoutExpired`), green
    after;
  - the EXISTING `test_commit_guard_fails_explicitly_when_head_times_out` and
    `test_session_finish_fails_explicitly_when_porcelain_times_out`, re-pointed at a **persistent**
    block, proving the guard still fails loudly and has not been silently weakened;
  - the EXISTING `test_head_detects_a_commit` and `test_guard_fails_a_test_that_commits`, proving a
    real HEAD move is still detected.
- `make lint` and `make typecheck`.
- `pytest tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py tests/unit/test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py tests/unit/test_api_surface_gate.py`.
- `workflow_dispatch` of `test.yml` on the fix branch, proving `sweep (macos, full suite)` passes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The cause is established with quoted evidence that distinguishes contention from a leaked
      process or handle, with the rejected reading ruled out by mechanism rather than by assumption.
- [ ] A transient probe stall no longer errors the test that happens to be running: a defect-seeded
      reproduction fails RED before the change and passes after.
- [ ] The guard is not weakened -- a real HEAD move is still detected and still fails the test, and
      a **persistent** probe timeout still raises loudly rather than silently passing, each proven by
      a test that fails if the property is removed.
- [ ] The failing e2e test is not skipped, marked, or excluded on macOS; it is left untouched.
- [ ] `sweep (macos, full suite)` passes in a `workflow_dispatch` run of `test.yml` against the fix.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the mechanism-delta, predates-gate-parity and api-surface
      gate tests all pass.
